To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a force threshold-based position controller is presented for legged locomotion on irregular terrain, that it is robust to terrain elevation and that it is applied to a hexapod robot and a simulated hexapode walking blindly on irregular terrains.
the FTP controller has the ability to control a leg independently of the other legs, without the use of a multi-leg Jacobian.

1) the FTP controller can control the legs of a hexapod robot on irregular terrain without any information about the terrain or the state of the body; 2) the FTP controller has been successfully implemented on an experimental system, and has been tested on irregular terrain; and 3) the FTP controller also has been tested on different gaids without any modification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a new control architecture for legged robots.
the design, analysis, and experimental testing of a new class of control algorithms for the generation of robust, stable legged locomotion in complex and unstructured terrain.
the development of a control algorithm to enable legged vehicles to operate on unmodeled, irregular terrain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FTP controller can be used to generate a wide variety of legged locomotion on natural and irregular terrain.
the FTP controller can provide a simple, robust, and versatile method for controlling the locomotion of a hexapod robot.
this controller is robust and simple, and is applicable for walking on irregular terrain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a novel, simple, and robust controller that can control legged locomotion on irregular terrain, without using body feedback, or any knowledge of terrain.
the FTP controller has the potential to be used for legged robots with a wide range of body and leg configurations, and can be applied to different gaits without any modification.
the FTP controller provides a new paradigm for legged control that is simple and robust, while still being capable of complex behaviors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
force threshold comparison is a powerful method for controlling legged robots.
the FTP controller has the potential to be a general purpose, robust, and scalable control algorithm that is applicable across many legged platforms and gaits.
force feedback alone is sufficient to control the locomotion of a legged vehicle over natural terrain.
